## SECTION I – PRACTICE DIRECTIONS SUPPLEMENTING PART 52

## 1.1 There are five Practice Directions supplementing Part 52 –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 1.1 There are five Practice Directions supplementing Part 52 –] PD 52A – Appeals: general provisions

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 1.1 There are five Practice Directions supplementing Part 52 –] PD 52B – Appeals in the county courts and the High Court

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 1.1 There are five Practice Directions supplementing Part 52 –] PD 52C – Appeals to the Court of Appeal

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 1.1 There are five Practice Directions supplementing Part 52 –] PD 52D – Statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 1.1 There are five Practice Directions supplementing Part 52 –] PD 52E – Appeals by way of case stated

## SECTION II – INTRODUCTION

## 2.1 These Practice Directions apply to all appeals to which Part 52 applies. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 2.1 These Practice Directions apply to all appeals to which Part 52 applies.] 2.2 Part 52 complements the provisions of sections 54 to 57 of the Access to Justice Act 1999 and provides a uniform procedure for appeals in the county courts and the High Court and a modified procedure for the Civil Division of the Court of Appeal. Part 52 does not apply to –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 2.1 These Practice Directions apply to all appeals to which Part 52 applies.] (a) family proceedings in the High Court or county courts but does apply to appeals to the Court of Appeal from decisions made in family proceedings with such modifications as may be required;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 2.1 These Practice Directions apply to all appeals to which Part 52 applies.] (b) appeals in detailed assessment proceedings against the decision of an authorised court officer. ## SECTION III – DESTINATIONS OF APPEAL

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > SECTION III – DESTINATIONS OF APPEAL] 3.1 Section 56 of the Access to Justice Act 1999 enables the Lord Chancellor to specify the destinations of appeal in different cases. The Access to Justice Act 1999 (Destinations of Appeal) Order 2016 specifies the general destinations of appeal which apply subject to any statutory provision to the contrary. Appeals in respect of individual insolvency and corporate insolvency proceedings are specified in section 375 of the Insolvency Act 1986 and rule 7.47 of the Insolvency Rules 1986 respectively. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > SECTION III – DESTINATIONS OF APPEAL] The destinations of appeal provided by these provisions are explained in the following paragraphs of this section of this Practice Direction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > SECTION III – DESTINATIONS OF APPEAL] 3.2 ‘Statutory appeals’ and ‘Appeals by way of case stated’ are dealt with in PD52D – refer to those provisions for the appropriate court to which such an appeal may lie. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > SECTION III – DESTINATIONS OF APPEAL] 3.3 The court or judge to which an appeal is to be made (subject to obtaining any necessary permission) is set out in the tables below–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > SECTION III – DESTINATIONS OF APPEAL] Table 1 deals with appeals in proceedings other than family and insolvency proceedings;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > SECTION III – DESTINATIONS OF APPEAL] Table 2 deals with appeals in insolvency proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > SECTION III – DESTINATIONS OF APPEAL] Table 3 deals with appeals in family proceedings which may be heard in the Family Division and to which the CPR may apply. ## 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘Destination’: the court to which the appeal lies. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘DJ’: District judge. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘CJ’: Circuit judge including a recorder. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘CJ (CC)’: Circuit judge in the county court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] “DC”: a Divisional Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘Master’: Master, district judge sitting in a district registry or any other judge referred to in article 4 of the Destination of Appeals Order. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘HCJ’: single judge of the High Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘HCJ(FD)’: single judge of the family Division of the High Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘CA’: Court of Appeal. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘Companies Acts’ means the Companies Act 1985, the Companies Act 1989 and the Companies Act 2006. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] ‘Registrar’: a Registrar in Bankruptcy, including a salaried or fee paid Registrar in Bankruptcy

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] “SC”: the Supreme Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] (Note: Tables 1, 2 and 3 do not include so-called ‘leap frog’ appeals either to the Court of Appeal pursuant to section 57 of the Access to Justice Act 1999 or to the Supreme Court pursuant to section 13 of the Administration of Justice Act 1969.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] 3.5 The destinations in the tables set out below apply in relation to first appeals, whether the decision is interim or final. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.4 Definitions of terms and abbreviations used in Tables 1, 2 and 3 –] (For a second appeal (an appeal from a decision of the County Court or the High Court which was itself made on appeal), the destination is the Court of Appeal (save where section 13 of the Administration of Justice Act 1960 applies, or the original decision was a decision of an officer authorised to assess costs by the Lord Chancellor: see article 6 of the Access to Justice Act 1999 (Destination of Appeals) Order 2016).)

## 3.6 Omitted. ## 3.7 Omitted. ## 3.8 Omitted. ## Filing appellant’s notice in wrong court

## 3.9

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.9] (1) Where a party attempts to file an appellant’s notice in a court which does not have jurisdiction to issue the notice, a court officer may notify that party in writing that the appeal court does not have jurisdiction in respect of the notice. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.9] (2) Before notifying a person under paragraph (1) the court officer must confer –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.9] (a) with a judge of the appeal court; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.9] (b) where the Court of Appeal is the appeal court, with a court officer who exercises the jurisdiction of that Court under rule 52.24. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 3.9] (3) Where a court officer, in the Court of Appeal, notifies a person under paragraph (1), rule 52.24(5) and (6) shall not apply. ## SECTION IV – OBTAINING PERMISSION TO APPEAL AND ALLOCATION OF APPEALS

## Definitions

## 4.A1 Definitions of terms used in this Section—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.A1 Definitions of terms used in this Section—] ‘heard’: in the context of an application, includes dealing with that application on paper as well as orally. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.A1 Definitions of terms used in this Section—] ‘Group A Judge’: a High Court Judge or a person authorised under paragraphs (1), (2) or (4) of the Table in section 9(1) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 to act as a judge of the High Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.A1 Definitions of terms used in this Section—] ‘Group B Judge’: any person who is not a Group A Judge but who is authorised under section 9 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 to act as a judge of the High Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.A1 Definitions of terms used in this Section—] ‘Group C Judge’: a person authorised under paragraphs (4A) or (5) of the Table in section 9(1) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 to act as a judge of the High Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.A1 Definitions of terms used in this Section—] ‘Group D Judge’: a person authorised under paragraph (6) of the Table in section 9(1) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 or section 9(4) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 to act as a judge of the High Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.A1 Definitions of terms used in this Section—] ‘Registrar’: a Registrar in Bankruptcy, including a salaried or fee paid Registrar in Bankruptcy. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.A1 Definitions of terms used in this Section—] ‘The Appropriate Presiding or Supervising Judge’ means the relevant Supervising judge of the Business and Property Courts or relevant Presiding judge of the King’s Bench Division, and includes the Chancellor of the High Court, the Judge in Charge of the King’s Bench List, and the President of the King’s Bench Division. ## Where to apply for permission

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > Where to apply for permission] 4.1 An application for permission to appeal in proceedings which are not contempt proceedings or from the CA may be made–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > Where to apply for permission] (a) to the lower court at the hearing at which the decision to be appealed against is given (in which case the lower court may adjourn the hearing to give a party an opportunity to apply for permission to appeal); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > Where to apply for permission] (b) where the lower court refuses permission to appeal or where no application is made to the lower court, to the appeal court in accordance with rule 52.12. ## Form

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > Form] 4.2 An application for permission to appeal to the appeal court must be made using an appellant’s notice (form N161 or N164 (small claims track)). ## Appeals from Masters, Registrars and District Judges of the High Court

## 4.3 In relation to appeals from Masters—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.3 In relation to appeals from Masters—] (a) applications for permission to appeal must be heard by a Group A Judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.3 In relation to appeals from Masters—] (b) if permission to appeal is given, the appeal may be heard by a Group A Judge or a Group B Judge authorised to hear the appeal by the Judge in Charge of the King’s Bench List or the Chancellor of the High Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.3 In relation to appeals from Masters—] 4.3A In relation to appeals from Registrars: applications for permission to appeal and appeals must be heard by a Group A Judge. ## 4.3B In relation to appeals from District Judges of the High Court:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.3B In relation to appeals from District Judges of the High Court:] (a) applications for permission to appeal must be heard by a Group A Judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.3B In relation to appeals from District Judges of the High Court:] (b) if permission to appeal is given, the appeal may be heard by either:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.3B In relation to appeals from District Judges of the High Court:] (i) a Group A Judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.3B In relation to appeals from District Judges of the High Court:] (ii) a Group C Judge sitting in the High Court; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.3B In relation to appeals from District Judges of the High Court:] (iii) in exceptional circumstances, a Group D Judge authorised to hear the appeal by the Appropriate Presiding or Supervising Judge. ## Appeals from the County Court to the High Court

## 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (a) subject to sub-paragraph (b)—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (i) applications for permission to appeal must be heard by a Group A Judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (ii) if permission to appeal is given:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (A)where the appeal is from a Recorder, the appeal may be heard by either a Group A Judge or, in exceptional circumstances, a Group C Judge authorised to hear the appeal by the Appropriate Presiding or Supervising Judge;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (B)in all other cases, the appeal may be heard by either a Group A Judge or, in exceptional circumstances, a Group D Judge authorised to hear the appeal by the Appropriate Presiding or Supervising Judge. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (b) where the appeal is from a District Judge in proceedings brought pursuant to the Companies Acts, an appeal to the High Court will be dealt with as follows—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (i) applications for permission to appeal must be heard in accordance with the following provisions:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (A)if the appeal centre is the RCJ, by a salaried Registrar in Bankruptcy; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (B)in any other appeal centre, by a Group C Judge or Group A Judge provided that the judge is one who could hear the appeal in accordance with sub-paragraph (iii). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (ii) for appeals in which the appeal centre is the RCJ: appeals must be heard by a Registrar;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (iii) for appeals in any other appeal centre: appeals may be heard by a Group A Judge or a Group B Judge, provided that—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (A) the Group A Judge is a judge of allocated to the Insolvency and Companies List of the Business and Property Courts or is authorised by the Chancellor of the High Court to hear the appeal;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (B) if the Group B judge is a Group D Judge, they have been authorised by the Supervising Judge of the Business and Property Courts to hear the appeal;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (C) if the Group B Judge is a Group C Judge, they have appropriate authorisation. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > 4.4 Where the lower court is the County Court—] (Note: the Practice Direction Insolvency Proceedings makes provision for obtaining permission to appeal and allocation of appeals in insolvency proceedings.)

## Appeals within the County Court

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 52A – APPEALS > Appeals within the County Court] 4.5 The Designated Civil Judge in consultation with the appropriate Presiding or Supervising Judge has responsibility for allocating appeals from decisions of District Judges in the County Court to Circuit Judges and/or Recorders. Such an appeal may only be allocated to a Recorder in exceptional circumstances.
